description: End-to-end scenario specifications with partial executable model evidence where noted. Structural checking is not execution.

scenarios.title: Letter through two relays and carried media
steps: Prepare a native signed letter offline with a stable Message-ID and two groups.
Accept locally, lose the reply, and retry.
Durably queue work for relay-a. Exercise an actual BPv7 contact outage and sender restart; restore contact, lose the application receipt, restart the receiver, and retry.
Resume through relay-b and carried media; import overlapping batches.
Commit matching release evidence while retaining independent archive pins.
expected: One article and one allocation per intended local membership.
Recovery restores obligations and permits receipt regeneration.
Local numbers may differ; transport reception does not imply human reading.
Bundle lifetime, expiry and transport status cannot release an fn application or archive obligation; destructive BPA deletion occurs only after durable fn staging.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: actual two-node fn/BPv7 letter and return-receipt exchange, outage/restart, lost receipt and distinct-BID duplicate with one article/pin per node. Native signatures, two relays and carried-media composition remain open.

scenarios.title: Atomic cross-post and duplicate acceptance
steps: Prepare a two-group acceptance and observe before/after commit.
Retry the same identity and attempt a conflicting binding.
On the committed Store, compare an identical payload and ordered groups, then change payload, groups, and Message-ID separately.
expected: No partial membership is visible.
Retries allocate no numbers and do not overwrite accepted bytes.
Message-ID comparison is exact.
scenarios.execution_scope: Validated for abstract atomic acceptance; the native path is one article posted to two groups through the operator, one local number in each group across a restart, an identical resubmission accepted as the duplicate and a changed source under the held Message-ID refused without replacing the stored octets (tests/test_native_conformance.py). The charged pin is not observed by that case. The Python-host implementation (tests/test_store.py) retired with the Python host.

scenarios.title: Crash matrix around durable acceptance
steps: Crash at each object-write, namespace/barrier, commit-record, publication, and reply boundary.
Allow unsynced writes to tear/reorder within the selected model.
Recover and retry.
Exercise the fresh initializer with configuration history and repeated fresh staging names, and separate a removed configuration-directory fence from the root/transactions relation.
At native transaction recovery, supply a malformed final filename, a canonical filename hard-linked to a differently sequenced record, and a namespace exceeding its physical observation budget.
At native configuration recovery, supply a decoded-generation/basename mismatch, a canonical-looking symlink, a duplicate or gap, malformed bytes, and an entry beyond the physical observation budget.
expected: Modeled acknowledged commits survive; complete unacknowledged commits may survive.
No partial transaction is published.
Uncertainty fences mutations; platform assumptions are recorded.

Fresh successful initialization reaches the full image including durable configuration history; a weaker relation alone is not evidence of that publication. Transaction names come from the attached ACL2 renderer and remain distinct for distinct natural sequences.
Bound enumeration before retaining excess names; ACL2 owns canonical names and contiguous sequence pairs, and each decoded record must match its issued sequence before replay.

The configuration observer retains every bounded physical entry until ACL2 has decoded it and bound its generation to the canonical name. A conflicting, malformed, gapped, duplicate, excess, unreadable, or non-regular entry faults recovery rather than being filtered into a shorter history.
scenarios.execution_scope: Mixed actual node/file trace retention and observed replay/barrier gates have targeted certification. Forty-seven injection rows, six process-death cuts and sixteen malformed-image cases exercise the adapter. These finite tests do not qualify physical power loss or whole-store rollback. The deploy gate adds one real process-death cut on a farm box (SIGKILL from inside an open POST, recovery, reread); it is one point of the matrix, not the matrix, and a SIGKILL is not a power loss. W13 adds exact fresh-initializer image and transaction-name component evidence. Existing/retry initialization, native execution correspondence and coverage of every syscall/death cut remain open. W18 adds explicit existing-valid and history-fenced retry programs with EEXIST observations, plus source-pinned native repeated-init and SIGKILL/reopen tests. Non-EEXIST publication errors are uncertain. These are selected branch/runtime results, not whole-host or power-loss correspondence; the followup classifier covers expected-EEXIST links, and separate link/barrier handlers preserve uncertainty for post-link errors. Integrated raw-handler tests also exercise the named post-link error cut. Whole-image validation of these later corrections remains separate. Native U13 has source-matched developer Store-image malformed-name and sequence-binding witnesses plus raw observation bounds; it is not a full production-image, configuration-history or power-loss result.

scenarios.title: Checkpoint and complete index reconstruction
steps: Commit articles, allocations, obligations, receipts, and policy context.
Checkpoint and replay its suffix; rebuild indexes.
Compare exact lookups and ranges with full replay.
expected: All future-relevant state is preserved.
Range results are complete, not just individually valid.
Checkpoint choice does not depend on wall-clock recency.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: logical checkpoint/suffix equivalence and index reconstruction are certified. Source-pinned native tests cover capture/select/reopen, selected corruption without rollback, unselected isolation, byte-identical cross-open, namespace bounds and selected crash cuts. The namespace successor adds unconditional mismatch corruption and mutation fencing. Recovery still fully replays the journal and compares a private restore; suffix-only recovery, full owner/index integration and every-cut physical correspondence remain open. A source-pinned ACL2 selected-pack witness additionally reconstructs E2 history/incarnation/sequence and bound hybrid keyring/historical verdict from exact event bytes; the version-two recovery-only checker also compares topic projection and the rebuilt consumer sequence index, rejecting mismatches. Combined native checkpoint/consumer/T10 reopen remains open.

scenarios.title: Interrupted compaction with active readers
steps: Create independent roots and pin a read on an old segment.
Compact under temporary-space pressure.
Crash around replacement publication and old-segment reclamation.
expected: Protected dependencies and evidence survive.
No-space causes safe refusal, not forced deletion.
Active readers retain required bytes; history policy persists.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: selected lossless prefix packs reconstruct exact Store event bytes; focused tests cover corruption, missing selected authority, crash after a prefix unlink, resumed reclamation, and suffix replay. A certified pack-retirement plan excludes selected authority and models arbitrary survival after issued unlinks. Native source tests cover pack-retirement cuts, retry, exact source preservation, and active-reader refusal; pack-retirement awaits a source-matched developer image. The b074f94e developer-image fixture confirms active-reader exclusion before pack-reclaim unlink and exact source/retention preservation after release, reclamation and reopen (planning/evidence/checkpoint-active-reader-b074-2026-09-24.md). General concurrent physical reclamation, article-object reclamation, every physical cut, and filesystem qualification remain open.

scenarios.title: Corruption and old valid snapshots
steps: Inject detectable corruption in referenced content and committed metadata.
Attempt reading/recovery.
Separately replace the whole store by an older internally valid snapshot.
expected: Detected damage follows an explicit fault/repair path.
Damaged content cannot generate fresh success.
Rollback detection is claimed only with an independent freshness anchor.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: actual checksum/truncation/unknown-schema/gap/symlink faults refuse recovery; replacement by a whole valid old store is intentionally undetected without an external anchor.

scenarios.title: Capacity refusal and indefinite local retention
steps: Fill the configured article/metadata reservation budget.
Attempt new work.
Advance wall time without authorization, then release one eligible archive pin.
expected: Unaffordable work is refused before acceptance.
Local archive pins do not expire automatically.
One release does not discharge unrelated obligations.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: ledger and node retention proofs, real adapter bounds/maximum-profile replay, and BP receiver capacity refusal preserving prior article/archive pin. No durable deletion/compaction or physical disk-reservation proof.

scenarios.title: Lost, stale, and mismatched receipts
steps: Persist a successor undertaking and drop its reply.
Restart, retry, and regenerate the receipt.
Inject duplicates and wrong-subject/issuer/incarnation receipts.
expected: Undertakings do not multiply or vanish on restart.
Only matching sufficient authorized evidence permits discharge.
Socket ACKs and transmission reports do not release obligations.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: actual receiver undertaking and receipt decision survive reopen; distinct-BID duplicate regenerates identical receipt and real BP returns it to a durably reopened sender. Five actual receiver SIGKILL cuts verify exact staged request/article, single record/article/pin, explicit pending recovery and identical receipts. Joint sender binding and fixed-Store receiver decision/replay/receipt-byte invariants are certified with nonvacuity and rejected-extension cases. Authenticated remote evidence, changing-Store composition and general journal-byte/host refinement remain open. The later native owner/FNRJ join independently exercises death after durable decision and before receipt authorship, then exact receipt replay after restart/retransmit without additional Store transaction/article/pin. Earlier fixed-Store theorems do not by themselves prove the new evolving-Store host composition. A later actual receipt-decision namespace-barrier EIO case observes uncertain exit with no receipt, then fresh-process recovery and exact receipt replay without additional Store acceptance.

scenarios.title: Reordered overlapping partial batches
steps: Import overlapping batches in several orders with duplicates.
Delay dependencies and resume partial objects.
Include competing claims under one news identity.
expected: Validated fact sets converge under stated hypotheses.
Incomplete dependency closure has no complete-acceptance receipt.
Local policies/numbers may differ and conflict evidence persists.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: four-node validated fact merging/conflicts plus bounded volatile object assembly with reordered fragments, duplicates, gaps, conservative overlap conflict, byte/fragment/metadata limits and explicit empty candidates. No persistent transfer, selected portable batch grammar, dependency closure or acceptance receipts.

scenarios.title: Long asymmetric contacts and clock jumps
steps: Queue letters and receipts during a long outage.
Offer a brief one-way contact using cached inventory, then a return contact.
Jump wall time and vary permitted capacity/fairness.

After two durable local BP receives, make the older carrier clock-uncertain while the newer carrier is live; select and deliver the newer without changing the older. Also leave only the uncertain carrier, and separately make the FNBS publication outcome uncertain.
expected: Useful bounded batches need no preliminary dialogue.
Clock jumps do not discharge promises or prove non-delivery.
Progress assumptions and BP/fn lifetime distinctions are explicit.
Per-carrier clock uncertainty does not block a different live local delivery, while an uncertain publication still fences mutation.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: real queued BP delivery after contact outage and process restart, sender retry semantics and finite transport-safety proofs. The local A3 clocked selector has a certified two-receive ACL2 trace, with no source-matched native image for that change. Asymmetric scheduled windows, wall-clock jumps, LTP and fairness/liveness remain open.

scenarios.title: Restore incarnations and forks
steps: Issue origin events and retain an older backup.
Restore/clone that backup after more events circulate.
Attempt issuance and exchange competing histories.
expected: Restore discipline prevents unrecognized identity reuse under A-IDENTITY.
Fork evidence remains; timestamps do not settle authority.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: ACL2 clone proposal/phase tests certify, and native source implements a pre-open fence, no-replace cold copy and durable rollover/reopen. The saved-image fixture and process-death cuts are written but await a combined E2 image; competing origin forks and served cursor rejection remain open.

scenarios.title: Source variants, signatures, and authority
steps: Import native signed content, gateway provenance, and legacy wire variants.
Change Path/Xref and gateway injection projections while keeping exact authored source octets, including unknown allowed headers and MIME bytes; separately alter signed source content.
Present unrelated signatures and forged administrative requests.

Render the selected FN-Authorship carrier from independently supplied Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 keys, verify the received article, then alter one exact source byte and one encoded public-key byte separately.
expected: Provenance categories remain distinct.
The selected signing preimage binds exact authored source bytes. Changing mutable projections does not rewrite those bytes; changing authored content is not a projection-only change.
Relay mutation and authored conflict are distinguished; unrelated signers gain no authority.
The portable verifier accepts only the intact both-signature artifact and refuses each altered variant; its result is distinct from a Store historical verdict.
scenarios.design_note: D01 selects this source boundary and the FN-Authorship v1 carrier implements a bounded portable artifact check. The native CLI source/keyset mutation witness covers only that check; Store binding, served HDR and peer transit remain open.

scenarios.title: Codec vectors and hostile declarations
steps: Round-trip schema boundary values.
Supply duplicate keys, alternate encodings, truncation, huge lengths, deep nesting, and unknown versions.
Compare bytes with an independent implementation.
expected: Accepted values have the specified deterministic encodings.
Resource checks precede allocation; input is never evaluated as Lisp.
Unknown schemas cannot establish semantic authority.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: primitive/schema-0 round trips and accepted-input canonicality, 38 independent cbor2 cases, malformed-store vectors, exact article preservation/recognized bounded syntax, semantic fields, UTF-8/wildmat correspondence, and CBOR/record guards. Native/batch/signature schema and full public resource proofs remain open.

scenarios.title: NNTP cursor, capabilities, and framing
steps: Exercise advertised forms with a real reader and independent transcripts.
Partition CRLF, dot terminators, and articles across socket chunks.
Exercise empty/missing groups, IDs, cursors, ranges, wildmat, failed selection, and oversized input.

Poll with NEWNEWS over a wildmat and a date, with and without GMT and with both year forms, against stamped articles whose payloads carry Injection-Date, Date, and neither, plus carried-over legacy articles.
expected: Capability claims match the audited profile.
Cursor/errors follow the checklist.
Socket partitions do not change meaning; rejected body tails do not become commands.

NEWNEWS names exactly the matching groups' articles at or after the requested acceptance stamp or conservative legacy horizon, without reading payloads or a size refusal; syntax and two-digit-year clock refusals stay distinct.
scenarios.execution_scope: Implemented reader session/cursor and effect shape have general proofs; exact ACL2 bridge input partitions and real reconnects have targeted tests. Full READER/POST and complete RFC byte-response conformance remain open. Framing and cursor coverage moved from the host to books/served, which states chunk-partition independence of the function the host calls. The capabilities leg is REFUTED as it stands: the deploy gate found POST answered with 340 while CAPABILITIES omits POST (RFC 3977 section 5.2.2).

scenarios.title: Host replay, stale completion, and backpressure
steps: Replay traces in the model simulator and core/host integration.
Deliver stale/duplicate completions.
Force partial output and stalled readers.

Install and exercise the native CLI and two native nodes without a Python runtime; include startup, concurrent NNTP posting/peering, control/reconfiguration, BP work, selected identity/anchor operations and crash recovery.
Record native image/source/dependency identities and child-process executions; distinguish an external test harness from either deployed node.

With two native owner clients already connected, inject uncertainty after publication on one client while the other attempts further input; then exercise shared-resource shutdown and independent recovery.
Start two distinct Store roots with one control socket path; issue concurrent native control posts and then repeat SIGTERM while NNTP and partial control clients are connected.
Send control frames in one-byte fragments and stall them; exceed the active control-client ceiling while a valid client continues; drop a post reply after durable completion and reopen independently.

On production default and DTN images, invoke raw store ROOT post with fresh and existing Store roots and an observable payload path; attempt a runtime profile override. Repeat raw insertion on the developer image, then exercise ordinary operator/NNTP posting, inspection and recovery on production.
expected: Stale completions cannot publish another transaction.
Finishing writes does not rerun semantic transitions.
Effects remain bounded and the same core/declared trust boundary is used.
No deployed entry point, helper or recovery path requires Python or silently falls back to the Python owner; missing native features remain open.
The native owner calls the same ACL2 semantic subjects or named justified refinements and preserves accepted, refused, uncertain and fault outcomes.

The uncertainty fence is established before releasing the shared mutex; no connected or newly arriving client mutates the stopped owner, workers finish before shared resources close, and the process reports uncertainty distinctly from a core fault.

A live store prepare may omit repeated history replay only through a named equality to fn-sn-prepare whose invariant is established at observed open and preserved by every post-open mutator; the shared owner additionally requires a named equality to its actual configured-owner event and exact preservation of owner/configuration context.

Only the endpoint lease holder receives control submissions; shutdown wakes clients without closing descriptors beneath their workers, joins before releasing resources, and permits independent reopen.

Control transport bounds active clients and total frame time, bounds allocation before consuming excess bytes, and accumulates input in linear work; a lost post reply is uncertain and a retry cannot duplicate durable acceptance.

Production raw insertion exits 5 as an unsupported entry before Store or payload I/O, regardless of a runtime profile override; no publication occurs. Developer raw insertion remains available. Ordinary production submission still injects and preserves its accepted/refused/uncertain contract, and production inspection/recovery remain available. This selected 2026-09-23 requirement is not yet implemented or witnessed by da5fd8cb.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: frozen03 default/DTN builds and scoped native suites passed, including public operator startup and concurrent uncertainty fencing. Later logical traces and targeted native tests cover stated subcontracts. The standalone store and shared-owner prepare projections are certified equal to their replaying specification/previous owner event under maintained relations, with nonempty-history witnesses and stale-node counterexamples when the premises are removed. A production image at 8cbeda9 passed all six targeted native-owner tests, including durable POST/reopen and uncertainty fencing. The frozen cdbd6b2 Python service matrix retains its recorded authentication and BP-crash disagreements. Full native service parity, deployment dependency evidence, concurrent backpressure/stale-completion composition and complete physical adapter correspondence remain open; the targeted owner image is not the whole deployment gate. The integrated control packet has ACL2 closure and exact-raw Darwin lifecycle/posting evidence; its saved-image build returned nonzero due to unrelated certificate origins, so it is not a clean native build gate. The later control resource packet passed scoped native slow-drip and active-client ceiling cases; it adds linear accumulation by source inspection, with the combined image gate still separate.

scenarios.title: History pruning and ancient reimport
steps: Release an eligible archive pin while retaining history.
Apply selected pruning rules and reimport old carried media.
Try to reuse an allocated local article number.
expected: Reimport follows the explicit resurrection/admissibility policy.
No other article reuses an allocation.
Independent obligations and evidence survive visibility changes.

scenarios.title: BP adapter acceptance separation
steps: Carry a real versioned batch through a selected BP implementation.
Observe transport status before application acceptance.
Expire a bundle or interrupt its path and retry.
Receive a nonzero fragment, restart, then receive offset zero and reassemble only from a complete coherent live family.
Reopen an FNWF journal interleaving ION route/observation records with application attempt, receipt and release records.
expected: Transport status is not a retention undertaking.
Only validated complete application inputs receive matching receipts.
No fragment enters Store before durable whole-bundle replacement; expired or unknown-age source rows cannot be silently omitted from that replacement.
Adapter version, lifetime profile, and interoperability evidence are recorded.

Successful mixed-journal replay preserves application work status with one restart, while ION observations remain separate from receipt/release authority; PRF-034 actual-caller correspondence is still open.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial: the actual pinned BPA exchange carries an experimental whole-article ADU and matching receipt through outage/restart/lost receipt/duplicate retry. Sender and receiver logical assurance and five receiver process-death cuts have separate evidence. Complete portable batches, explicit expiry/contact/quota cases, authenticated handoff and additional CLA profiles remain open. Moved to M4 to match the user's A06 active BP path; status remains specified. Native TCPCL request-to-owner-Store-to-receipt composition has a separate loopback restart witness; it is not external BPA interoperability or a complete contact-plan test. The fragment-carrier and observation-bound kind-18 transitions have ACL2 evidence; the two-process interrupted-fragment native fixture awaits a source-matched saved image. The optional offline ION sender has a certified ACL2 observation/route/replay component and a source-present native caller; native image qualification, real death/reopen and receipt-return over ION remain open.

scenarios.title: Private-profile design and crypto integration exercise
steps: Model trusted endpoints, opaque relay storage, and exposed metadata.
Walk through partitioned membership changes, delayed epochs, archive recovery, and secret-state rollback.
Compare candidate protocol requirements; later repeat using the selected implementation before shipping privacy.
expected: D04/D09 choices have an explicit threat model and no invented ratchet construction.
Ciphertext obligations do not require indefinite retention of all group secrets.
Membership ordering, signatures, archive recovery, and metadata leakage have separate stated semantics.
M1 evidence is a design exercise only; actual private-profile integration remains a later release gate.

scenarios.title: Two-node statement exchange through a peer that does not understand it
steps: Give node A and node B separate keyrings, both holding agent A's public key, and configure one relay between them that knows nothing about FN-Statement.
Agent A signs a statement over its authored source bytes and posts the article to node A with the statement in the FN-Statement header field.
Relay the article A -> relay -> B, capturing the octets at each hop.
On node B, fetch the article with ARTICLE and HEAD and verify the signature with an independent client that uses its own keyring and no fn code.
Ask node B for HDR :fn-verified over the article's range and over its Message-ID.
Repeat with the article's body altered by one octet in transit, with an article whose creator node B does not know, and with an article carrying no FN-Statement.
Offer node B a policy statement for a group the offering peer does not govern, then the genuine authority's policy statement, comparing the policy in force before and after each batch.
Have agent A reissue one (incarnation, sequence) slot with two different payloads, deliver one fork to each node, then peer the two nodes both ways.
Partition two sites, remove a different member at each, reconnect, and merge the reconnected peer's commits.
expected: The FN-Statement field arrives at node B byte-identical; only Path and Xref differ across the hops.
The independent client verifies the signature from the served bytes alone, without asking fn for a verdict.
HDR :fn-verified reports verified with the principal id in hex and the keyring generation under which the verdict was computed.

The altered body yields unverified ref-mismatch, the unknown creator unverified signature, and the missing field absent no-field; all three articles are still accepted, stored byte-exact and served, and no two of the outcomes render as one token.
The offering peer's policy statement leaves the policy in force equal before and after; the genuine authority's changes it, and the changing statement is named.
Both nodes end holding both forks and report the creator as an equivocator, with the durable equivocation record agreeing with the lace.
After the reconnection merge every earlier admit/refuse/hold decision is unchanged and the fork is exposed with both removals present.
No run here is proof evidence: it exercises the design's acceptance criteria against books that do not exist at this revision.

scenarios.title: A provenance survives the store, and a legacy one keeps its meaning
steps: Post one article to a fresh store; ACL2 decides the provenance from the live configuration and hands the host the form the record grammar accepts.
Close the store and reopen it, which replays the journal into a fresh node.
Ask the node for the provenance of that Message-ID and for the provenance of a value written before the typed record existed.
Ask for the provenance of a Message-ID the node does not hold.
expected: The stored evidence is the canonical wire form: prefixed, printable in octets 33 to 126, and at most 256 octets, so the host boundary guard and the record grammar both admit it.
The provenance read back after the reopen is the provenance the acceptance recorded, field for field.
A value written before the typed record existed reads back as the :legacy kind, verbatim, and renders as the string it always rendered as.
A Message-ID the node does not hold is a refusal (exit 1), distinct from uncertainty (exit 3) and a fault (exit 4).
scenarios.note: The transit path is NOT covered: it still stores fn-peer-evidence's rendering. See planning/lanes/HANDOFF-w10-provenance.md.

scenarios.title: Two peered nodes stand up, reconfigure live, and stop
steps: Initialize each node from the operator surface: a store, its served groups, and a configuration file naming the store, the listener and the ACL2 image.
Report each node's status; initialize over an existing store again; reject a wildcard listener configuration before bind with a usage result.
Create and retire a served group, and observe the created group over the socket.
Start each node's service, declare a group on the running service's control channel, and attempt the same change through the offline command while the service holds the store.
Stop each service and reopen each store.
expected: Every command's exit code distinguishes accepted, refused and uncertain, and no command reports an outcome the store did not take.
A configuration written by the operator surface is the one the service reads; nothing infers a store path from the working directory.
A change made while the service is live reaches the served configuration through the control channel, and the offline path is refused rather than racing it.
A stopped service releases the writer lock, and the store reopens without recovery.
scenarios.execution_scope: Specified. The v0 rows (planning/v0-matrix.json, last run b6759850) are owned by tests/test_native_conformance.py on one node and by tests/test_native_peering.py and tests/test_native_protected_peering.py between two nodes on one host over loopback (planning/evidence/python-diet-2-2026-09-28/v0-row-owners.md). Nothing here exercises two machines, a real network, or an operator's own configuration.

scenarios.title: AUTHINFO login and posting permission
steps: Derive a principal from a seed and record an AUTHINFO credential for it on each node.
Connect unauthenticated and read the advertised capabilities; attempt a gated command.
Authenticate with AUTHINFO USER and PASS, read the capabilities again, and post.
Authenticate with a wrong password on a fresh connection.
Run one complete served read with a nonempty no-posting credential list: AUTHINFO USER/PASS then local POST, and separately AUTHINFO USER/PASS then configured-peer TAKETHIS with an article body.
expected: AUTHINFO USER is advertised exactly while the connection is unauthenticated, and is withdrawn once it is not.
A gated command before the login is refused and not performed.
The posting allowance is the authenticated principal's, not the connection's.
A wrong password is refused and grants nothing; the refusal is distinct from a fault.

The no-posters served-read invariant excludes every local injected submission, but the independently authorized principal-bound transit path may emit a typed peer submission; removing the no-posters premise allows a complete accepted local POST.
A policy-switched pending POST state can submit despite a no-posters credential policy, but cannot arise from an initial no-posters connection under the proved fold invariant.
scenarios.execution_scope: Partial native evidence: startup loads bounded credential verifiers, required unauthenticated command returns 480, wrong password returns 481, correct password returns 281 and subsequent GROUP succeeds; authenticated reader IHAVE remains 502. Protected-only startup and legacy cleartext credential files refuse. Login transport is unprotected loopback, so no confidentiality claim follows. Native credential enrollment, TLS, reload and full cross-node scenario remain separate. The served-fold distinction between local POST and authorized transit is ACL2-certified with reachable complete-read witnesses; no new native transcript is claimed by that component evidence.

scenarios.title: Transit between two peered fn nodes in both directions
steps: Peer each node with the other by a record naming its path-identity, its transport and its inbound and outbound wildmats.
Establish the control: each node serves its own article and refuses the other's.
Offer one article each way with IHAVE, then offer the same Message-ID a second time, then offer one whose Path already names the target.
Offer a further article each way with MODE STREAM, CHECK and TAKETHIS, and repeat the offer after the target holds it.
expected: A wanted offer draws 335 and then 235, and the target serves the source's octets with its own path-identity and the RFC 5537 section 3.2.1 diagnostic prepended to Path and every Xref removed, every other header and the body byte-identical (specs/peering.md 2.3); local article numbers may differ.
A second offer of a held Message-ID draws 435 and no second copy is written.
An article whose Path already names the target is refused after its 335 and is not served afterwards.
CHECK answers 238 for a wanted article and 438 for one the target holds; TAKETHIS answers 239 and 439 to match, never a 2xx and never a retry code.
A peer record is configuration, not authorization: nothing in this scenario authenticates the peer.
scenarios.execution_scope: A source-matched production image ran two native owners on one host over private loopback. Public operator configuration drove byte-identical A-to-B and B-to-A transfers, and each held Message-ID drew 435. A separate client reset while a transit completed; the target retained the article and stayed live, but the test did not observe whether the reply write itself failed. The run did not exercise TLS, two hosts, a partition, latency or clock disagreement, and two articles crossing once is not the merge property of specs/peering.md section 4.

scenarios.title: Owner-driven outbound feed
steps: Configure an outbound wildmat on a peer record and accept an article that matches it.
Let the owner open the session and offer the article; drive no socket by hand.
Reread the target after the acknowledgement, and again after the source restarts.
Interrupt an offer in flight and restart the owner.
Cut a following FNFD envelope at each byte boundary, reopen, append and reopen again.
Offer complete corrupt or wrong-peer FNFD evidence, and inject failed content/directory barriers.
expected: Each accepted article is offered to each peer whose outbound wildmat matches it, by the owner and not by an operator.
A transfer the target acknowledged is not offered again, and the target holds one copy.
The feed journal distinguishes transmission from retention, and survives the restart.
An interrupted offer is retried and produces no second copy.
Only a torn final envelope is truncated to the ACL2-returned safe offset; a later append remains replayable after another restart.
Complete invalid evidence remains unchanged; ambiguous I/O exits uncertain and the owner performs no later mutation or success response.
scenarios.execution_scope: The owner drives outbound feeds; the former standalone tools/run_feed.py is retired. A source-matched production image ran the combined public operator, owner, feed and inbound NNTP path over private loopback. It transferred one article byte-identically in each direction, suppressed both duplicates, and requeued a durable FNFD obligation after the source process was killed and restarted. W12 separately covers bounded journal replay and cuts. Article-commit/feed-intent atomicity and general K5 correspondence remain active work, so the whole scenario is not marked validated.

scenarios.title: A bundle each way over fn's own convergence layer
steps: Build the node image carrying the convergence layer and establish a contact between two of them.
Transfer one bundle each way inside one session, segmented by the layer's own rules.
Interrupt the contact and re-establish it; hold an idle contact open with the keepalive.
Carry an fn article inside a bundle and deliver it to the receiving node's application.
Inject errors at native lifecycle publication barriers, reopen, and distinguish a visible record from durable queue acceptance.
Reuse a session-local transfer ID in another inbound session with different content; retain both evidence records and fence all mutation after an uncertain journal write.
expected: The transfer is segmented and acknowledged by the layer's own rules, and the assertions are over the events the layer recorded.
A bundle's arrival is not an fn application acceptance, and the two are reported separately.
An interrupted contact retains durably queued work; transport retries may repeat a bundle, while application acceptance and obligation charging remain idempotent.
A refused contact is refused with its own reason, distinct from a fault.

scenarios.title: Articles over the protected feed between a Linux node and an OpenBSD node, both from release tarballs: posted on each side, read on the other, and a hybrid-signed carrier crossing once

Post one article on each node over STARTTLS; `peer pull` each way.

Neither node stops; a fault that stops one is a failure of this scenario, not an environment note.

status says open=checkpoint:S; the reopened owner serves the same; both VmHWM below the limit.

scenarios.title: The one resumable checkpoint pipeline: the automatic publication and the verb write the schema-3 tables in batches through the publication buffer, decided by name before any allocation; the file reopens as the full replay and the verb republishes it byte for byte
steps: A development-profile store (K = 128); an owner; 64 POSTs; connections until the owner logs `CHECKPOINT auto sequence=64 suffix=64 octets=N steps=T ms=M' with T >= 4 (one step per table at least); stop.

The source assertions: the thread calls fn-ock-next-checkpoint, fn-ockp-setup and the batch loop over the publication buffer; the verb calls fn-store-sco-publish-setup and the same loop; the open loads through fn-sct-load; the cut map is fn-bs-scp-program's, unchanged.

A fresh store under FN_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT_BUDGET_TEST=1024: the deferral line `CHECKPOINT deferred reason=exceeds-budget estimate=E budget=1024', nothing written, serving continues, no retry, `status' carries the deferral; a fresh owner under the profile's budget publishes at 66.

scenarios.title: A kill between two pipeline steps reopens with the old checkpoint (the `created' cut's verdict) and the staged file is swept by the writer's recover
steps: A development-profile store; an owner; 64 POSTs; the automatic publication at 64 (the old checkpoint, its digest kept); stop.
An owner under FN_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT_BATCH_FAULT=0:kill; 64 more POSTs; the owner is killed by its publication thread after the first step's frames were written.

The old checkpoint's bytes are unchanged; `status' reads open=checkpoint:64 suffix=64; `recover' sweeps the staging orphan; a fresh owner publishes at 128 and the next open reads open=checkpoint:128 suffix=0.

scenarios.title: A reader reads a cross-posted article's overview: the Xref field names the node's path-identity and the article's local number in every group that holds it, and LIST OVERVIEW.FMT names Xref:full

A reader: LIST OVERVIEW.FMT; GROUP fn.test; OVER 1-100; XOVER 1-100; OVER; OVER <msgid>; GROUP fn.alt; OVER 1-2; ARTICLE <msgid>.

scenarios.title: A certificate renewal reaches a running node by `tls reload`: new connections get the new certificate, an open session keeps working, and a mismatched key or a dropped name is refused by name with the old certificate still served
steps: `store init fn.test`; certificate A (SAN localhost) at tls/cert.pem and tls/key.pem; `run` with protected_only and a control socket; a reader completes STARTTLS and stays open; `status`.
Replace both files with pair B (SAN localhost, reload.localhost) by rename; a new reader handshakes; `tls reload`; a new reader handshakes; the open reader sends DATE; `status`.
Replace the key with one from another pair; `tls reload`; a new reader handshakes.
Install pair D (SAN localhost only); `tls reload`; a new reader handshakes; the open reader sends QUIT.
With no owner running, `tls reload`.
expected: The first reader is served A; `status` prints `tls names=localhost not-after=YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.

Before the reload the new reader is still served A; `tls reload` exits 0 and prints `tls names=localhost,reload.localhost not-after=...`; the next reader is served B; the open reader's DATE answers 111; `status` prints B's names.
`tls reload` exits 1 with `refused operator tls key-mismatch`; the new reader is served B.
`tls reload` exits 1 with `refused operator tls names-dropped`; the new reader is served B; QUIT answers 205 and the owner is still running.
The command exits non-zero and is not accepted.

scenarios.title: A hostile network is thrown at a running node: malformed command lines, header and body abuse, connection floods and slowloris, pipelining and transit storms, and raw TCPCL/BP abuse; the node stays up, answers a clean session throughout, holds memory bounded, and refuses every ill-formed input by name
steps: Start a scratch loopback owner under systemd-run (MemoryMax=8G) on the developer image; never the live node.
Per family (malformed, header, body, connection, pipelining, transit, bp) send bounded adversarial traffic and log the first line the node returned.

After each family run the oracle: a clean authenticated GROUP/DATE/LIST session answers, the owner is alive with RSS under the profile's heap figure, no served request exceeded the wall bound, and the service log holds no fault.
For BP, drive a bp-node serve listener with wrong TCPCL magic, a never-completing contact, and an XFER_SEGMENT declaring a 4 GiB payload with tiny data.
expected: Every malformed command line is refused 501; header/body abuse is refused 441 by a distinct named reason or accepted only when valid (a supplied Path is injected per NNT-012); a connection flood is refused 400 past the capacity and slowloris is closed silently at the timer; 1000 pipelined DATEs all answer and non-peer TAKETHIS/CHECK/IHAVE are refused 502; the bp-node answers an oversized XFER_SEGMENT with MSG_REJECT and does not preallocate the declared length.
The node never crashes, never hangs past its bounds, never grows memory without bound, and answers a clean session correctly after every family.
scenarios.execution_scope: Executed on hbox (developer image, code-identical to dev b4b343d51) against a scratch loopback owner and bp-node under systemd-run MemoryMax=8G. All seven families green, no defects. Not exercised: transit interior abuse (announced sizes, million-id promises, pipelined TAKETHIS/PKT-600) from an authenticated peer session (a non-peer connection is uniformly refused 502; the peer path is covered by SCN-138); a real 100 MiB body under a peer feed; TLS-port handshake garbage on 563 (no TLS listener configured in this run).

scenarios.title: The TLS surface of a running node is thrown hostile traffic on 563 (implicit TLS) and 119 (STARTTLS): garbage before and mid handshake, a hello with no cipher, TLS 1.0/1.1 only, an oversized record, plain NNTP on the TLS port, STARTTLS-then-plain-then-STARTTLS, an unsolicited client cert, an unserved SNI, alert and close_notify floods, a TLS-layer slowloris, and a full-handshake burst; the node refuses each by a named TLS alert or 502, serves a clean session throughout, and holds memory bounded
steps: Start a scratch loopback owner under systemd-run (MemoryMax=8G) on the dev-HEAD developer image, configured with a self-signed [listener] tls_cert/tls_key pair and a tls_port; never the live node.

Against the implicit-TLS port and the STARTTLS path, send the tls family: garbage before/mid handshake, a ClientHello with no cipher and a NULL cipher, TLS 1.0 and 1.1 only offers, a 16 KiB+1 record, plain NNTP on the TLS port, STARTTLS then plain then STARTTLS again, STARTTLS then garbage, an unsolicited client certificate, SNI for an unserved name, an alert flood, a close_notify storm, and a 200-way TLS slowloris.
Measure the handshake CPU cost: 300 sequential handshakes and a 30 s 48-way full-handshake burst, reading the owner's /proc CPU and thread count.

Run the oracle: a clean plaintext session answers, the owner is alive with RSS under the heap figure, no served request exceeded the wall bound, the service log holds no fault, the second STARTTLS is 502, a reader is served during the flood, and the implicit-TLS listener still answers afterward.
expected: Every hostile handshake is refused by a named TLS alert (record_overflow, illegal_parameter, handshake_failure, protocol_version, unexpected_message) or held to the 10 s deadline and closed; plain NNTP on the TLS port leaks no reply; the second STARTTLS is 502; unsolicited client certs and unserved SNI complete and are ignored (single cert served).

The node never crashes, hangs, or grows memory without bound; RSS stayed 585 MB under a 2,819 MB heap figure; steady-state node CPU 2.467 ms per handshake. Two host-level gaps are filed as packets: TLS handshakes are not metered by the exposure kernel (PKT-639) and TLS refusals are logged only to stderr, not the service log (PKT-640).
scenarios.execution_scope: Executed on hbox against the dev-HEAD developer image 6701d5753 (system libssl OpenSSL 3.3.1) and probed against a LibreSSL node on the OpenBSD VM, both loopback under systemd-run MemoryMax=8G; never the live node. TLS family green, no crash/hang/leak/fault; two host-level packets filed (PKT-639 unmetered handshakes, PKT-640 refusals not in service log). Not exercised: a real TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate flood (an encrypted post-handshake record, not forgeable with the standard library); the OpenBSD implicit-TLS (563) port (the VM node ran STARTTLS only).

scenarios.title: An offline configuration request authorizes from the fold its open computed: 300 separate `peer carries` requests timed against the image before PRF-209
steps: `operator CONFIG init`; `peer add far ...`; FN_PEER_ROWS_REQUESTS=300 separate `peer carries far HEX`, timed, on the image before and after PRF-209 on the same box; `operator CONFIG group create` answers `verification=VERIFIED` (tests.test_native_admin).

scenarios.title: Pipelined articles: eight TAKETHIS in one write from a streaming peer, and two POST blocks in one write from a reader, are each committed and answered in order
steps: Node T with peer S: eight TAKETHIS commands with their articles in one write; QUIT.
Node T with peer S: four TAKETHIS with no CHECK, sent as small TCP_NODELAY segments cut every 7 octets and inside every .CRLF terminator.
Node P, no peer: two POST blocks in one write; POST, then the article and the next POST in one write, then the last article and QUIT in one write.
expected: Eight 239s in order, each echoing its Message-ID, then 205; all eight stored byte-identical.
Four 239s in order, each echoing its Message-ID, then 205; all four stored byte-identical.
340 240 340 240 340 240 340 240 205 in that order (no 340 before the 240 of the article preceding it); all four stored.

scenarios.title: Power is cut to the block device under a committing node (dm-log-writes, ext4) at 1,281 write boundaries across POST commits, checkpoint capture, compaction, reclaim, a near-full store and a recovery cut again; every acknowledged POST is served byte-identical afterwards, no refusal becomes acceptance, no binding or number moves
steps: On hbox (Linux 6.11): a data and a log loop device under dm-log-writes, ext4 on the mapped device; the developer image's node on it (scale profile, small open suffix): init, POSTs with a mark in the log after every 240 and every known 441 refusal, two store compactions, retention set released-by-all-holders, store reclaim; references read from the uncut store to /dev/shm.

For each cut (an entry of the log and a mode: flush, prefix, subset of unflushed writes, or 4096-octet tears), rebuild the device, mount, e2fsck, recover, store inspect the lost-reply POSTs, start the owner, ARTICLE and OVER everything, re-POST the newest acknowledged Message-ID and a fresh one, status; rerun compact or reclaim for their cuts; for a fifth of the cuts, cut the recovery again under a second log.
Control cuts judge a POST whose writes all follow the cut as acknowledged; each must be caught. A barrier=0 run shows the fsync assumption is load-bearing.
scenarios.expected: No acknowledged POST missing or changed, no refused POST served, lost-reply POSTs whole or absent, recover/owner/status without fault, bindings and numbers stable, reclaim accounting whole, every control caught; on barrier=0 acknowledged POSTs are lost (the assumption broken, not fn).

scenarios.title: Draining a contact of N ready base jobs examines each job record once and answers the head scan's offers in order
steps: Queue N base jobs for one peer on its routed hop (N = 1,000 through the machine's own :enqueue records; N = 10,000 as copies of one queued job, above the 4,096-record ceiling).
Drain one contact, asking before every offer, with the head scan (fn-bpnj-contact-next) and with the cursor (fn-bpnjc-contact-next), driving each offer's outcome.
Count the job records each drain's asks examine and time both drains and the transitions alone (tools/bench/bp-drain-bench.lisp).
expected: Both drains offer the same N jobs in the same order.
The cursor's asks examine N records in all (the head scan's about 2N^2), and the cursor drain's wall less the transitions' is a small constant share.

scenarios.title: Articles of 2,000,000 lines and of one 4 MiB line are posted, served (ARTICLE, BODY), reopened and served again byte-identical at 1 MiB of control stack per thread and at the image's own 64 MiB, on the production and developer images
steps: init a store with --max-article-octets 8388608; start the owner with SBCL_USER_ARGS=--control-stack-size 1MB; POST an article of 2,000,000 body lines (every sixteenth a lone dot), ARTICLE and BODY it; POST an article whose body is one line of 4,194,304 octets and ARTICLE it; SIGTERM.
start the owner at the image's own stack on the same store (the reopen); ARTICLE both again; POST a second 2,000,000-line article and ARTICLE it; SIGTERM.
